# NetPulse

> Browser-based network measurement: download, upload, ping, jitter and
> bufferbloat, plus gaming-region latency, WebRTC/DNS leak exposure and
> streaming readiness. Localised into 13 languages. No account, no install.

Latency is not reported as raw time-to-first-byte. The edge endpoint's own
processing time is subtracted using the `Server-Timing` response header, and
where the edge exposes kernel TCP statistics that round-trip is reported
directly — it tracks ICMP to within about a millisecond. Throughput is bytes
divided by elapsed time over a steady-state window that excludes TCP slow
start; no percentile of the peak is ever substituted for the mean, so every
figure reconciles with the byte counter shown beside it.

Links below are relative, so they resolve against whichever origin serves this
file.

## Tools

- [Speed and bufferbloat test](/tr/hiz-testi): Download, upload, ping, jitter, and latency measured again under load to grade bufferbloat from A+ to D.
- [Gaming ping radar](/tr/oyun-ping-radari): Live round-trip measurement to region-pinned endpoints near the major competitive game regions.
- [WebRTC and DNS leak detector](/tr/dns-webrtc-sizinti-testi): Checks whether the browser exposes a local address via WebRTC and whether DNS-over-HTTPS is reachable.
- [Download time calculator](/tr/indirme-suresi-hesaplayici): Converts a file size and a line speed into a transfer duration.
- [Guide and FAQ](/tr/rehber-ve-sss): What bufferbloat is, how to get an accurate reading, and how Mbps relates to MB/s.
